outcome: Asthma-related health care use (hospitalizations, outpatient visits, emergency department visits, intensive care unit admission)
cohort: Pregnant women who delivered in 2011 with pre-existing asthma from the Korean National Health Insurance claim database (2009-2013) were enrolled, and compared with nonpregnant female asthmatic control subjects.
finding: Pregnancy profoundly affects asthma-related health care use in asthmatic patients, leading to more hospitalizations but fewer outpatient visits and prescriptions, while asthma exacerbation during pregnancy, when appropriately managed, is not associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, except for an increased risk of cesarean section.
mod_finding: Asthma exacerbation during pregnancy was significantly related to an increased rate of cesarean section (27.1% vs 18.9%, P <.001).
